questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of apple orchards in England
How to bake the perfect apple crumble
Whether apples are really good for us
Why many doctors don't like old proverbs
questions.why: Sam asks if eating an apple a day can actually have significant health benefits.

questions.q: What does the proverb “Don't judge a book by its cover” advise?
options: Read more books, even ones that look boring
Don't judge people by their looks
Actions matter much more than words
Always buy books with a good cover
questions.why: Sam says it advises people not to form opinions about people based on how they look.

questions.q: According to new research, which part of the apple is especially healthy?
options: The seeds
The juice
The core
The skin
questions.why: Neil says there are benefits especially with the skins on, which are full of fibre, vitamins and flavonoids.

options: Lower blood pressure and help brain and heart
Make apples taste sweeter and juicier
Stop apples going bad for several weeks
Give you more energy late at night
questions.why: They are known to reduce blood pressure and improve brain and heart health.

questions.q: Why does Dr Michael Mosley say an apple is 'not some exotic superfood'?
options: Because apples are too expensive for most
Because apples have no real health benefits
To show an ordinary fruit can be healthy
Because he much prefers eating blueberries
questions.why: He lists big benefits, then says it's not an exotic superfood: 'it's an apple'.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a way Dr Mosley eats apples?
options: Grated into porridge
Sliced with yoghurt
Baked
Made into juice
questions.why: He mentions snacking, porridge, yoghurt and baked apples, but not juice.

questions.q: What does Sam say about cooking apples?
options: It doesn't damage the healthy flavonoids
It removes all the vitamins
It makes them too sweet
It is the least healthy way to eat them
questions.why: She says cooking or baking apples doesn't damage those healthy flavonoids.

questions.q: How does Neil feel about apple crumble with custard being healthy?
options: He completely agrees
He's doubtful it helps you get in good shape
He thinks it's the healthiest dessert
He says he never eats it
questions.why: He says, 'I'm not so sure that's a way to get in good shape'.
